rows.speaker: Ebû Bekir Şu‘be ve Ya‘kūb
rows.claim: Shuʿba's transmission from ʿĀṣim and Yaʿqūb read the verb with fatḥ on kāf and doubled mīm, in the sense of completing the count.
rows.anchor: Âsım’dan Ebû Bekir Şu‘be rivayeti ve Ya‘kūb kıraatinde kâf’ın fethi ve mîm’in teşdîdiyle وَلِتُكَمِّلُوا۟ ٱلْعِدَّةَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wills ease, and requires completing the number of fasting days through performance or make-up fasting.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı Allah yüsr ister, bir de {وَلِتُكْمِلُوا۟ ٱلْعِدَّةَ} şehrin aded-i eyyâmına göre edâen veya kazâen savmın adedini ikmal eylemenizi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands seek magnification and reverence of God with praise for His guidance, and the gratitude expected of believers.
rows.anchor: size hidâyet etmesine veya hidâyet ettiğine hamd ederek Allah’a tekbir ve tâziminizi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On his preferred syntactic connection, the lām is not causal: the sense is that God wills you to complete the count, like the lām in 5:6 and 61:8.
rows.anchor: Bu rabta göre وَيُرِيدُ لِتُكْمِلُوا,وَلِتُكْمِلُوا۟ demektir ki “lâm”lar ta‘lîl olmayıp يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ [el-Mâide 5/6], يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطْفِـُٔوا۟ [es-Saff 61/8] âyetlerindeki “lâm”lar gibidir.

rows.speaker: sâhib-i Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf says reading the lām as causal, with an implied “He prescribed all this,” gives the ending a subtler and more eloquent structure.
rows.anchor: sâhib-i Keşşâf beyan eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The count is measured by individual days: each day's fast has its own cause, so make-up fasting matches missed days rather than requiring the whole month.
rows.anchor: Aded her günün kendi orucuna sebeb ve mi‘yâr olduğunu gösterir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the verse says to complete the count rather than the month, someone who misses several Ramadan fasts need not make up the entire month; the month's days are not one fast.
rows.anchor: ramazanda birkaç oruç yiyen kimsenin bütün şehri kazâ etmesi lâzım gelmez.

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the duty can change during the month, a minor reaching puberty becomes obligated, while one who loses the conditions of obligation is released.
rows.anchor: ramazanın içinde tehavvül-i teklif muteberdir. Ortasında bâliğ olanlar mükellef olduğu gibi, şerâit-i teklîfi zâyi‘edenlerden de sâkıt olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A resident who begins Ramadan and travels during it receives the travel concession, but the day on which he departs while fasting is not included.
rows.anchor: ramazan bidâyetinde mukīm olan kimse ramazan içinde sefere çıkarsa yine ruhsata mazhardır. Ancak oruçlu olarak çıktığı günü bu ruhsata dâhil olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single intention at the month's beginning can still make the whole month's fast valid, because witnessing Ramadan is a general cause of obligation.
rows.anchor: evvelinden tamamına bir niyet ile de oruç sahih olabilir. Çünkü şuhûd-ı şehr bir sebeb-i icmâlîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magnifying God means reverence expressed in belief, speech, and action: affirming divine unity and justice, confessing His names and attributes, and worshipping through commanded acts.
rows.anchor: “Allah’ı tekbîr”, esasen Allah’a tâzim demektir ki üç mâna ile olur: ‘Akd-i kalb, kavl, amel.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech and deeds are accepted only when grounded in faith; 17:19 likewise conditions a deed's being thanked upon the worker being a believer.
rows.anchor: meşkûriyyet-i sa‘y, mü’min olmak hâliyle takyid edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because faith underlies every worship and other acts have causes unrelated to Ramadan, the contextual takbir is an uttered glorification marking completion of the Ramadan count and Eid.
rows.anchor: bu tekbîrin aded-i ramazanı ikmâle müte‘allik olarak bayrama işaret olması ve buna evlâ olan da lafz-ı tekbîrin izhar edilmesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “upon what He guided you to” carries an implicit sense of praise, which explains why takbir is joined to God with ʿalā.
rows.anchor: Bu âyette tekbîrin عَلَىٰ ile sılalanması da ma‘nâ-yı hamdin tazmînine mebnî olduğundan buna pek münâsibdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may concern takbir at sighting the Shawwal crescent, while going to Eid prayer, or during its takbirs; it does not specifically select one or establish loudness as obligatory.
rows.anchor: Bunlardan birine delâlet-i mahsûsa yoktur.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly said Muslims should takbir upon seeing the Shawwal crescent and continue until their Eid celebration is over, citing the verse.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretlerinden rivayet olunuyor ki: “Müslümanlar şevvâl hilâline baktıklarında bayramlarından fâriğ oluncaya kadar tekbir almaları üzerlerine

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali, Ebû Katâde, İbn Ömer, Saîd b. Müseyyeb, Urve, Kāsım, Hârice b. Zeyd, Nâfi‘ b. Cübeyr b. Mut‘im and other Companions
rows.claim: Reports say these Companions and early Muslims took takbir when setting out for the prayer ground on Eid.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali, Ebû Katâde, İbn Ömer, Saîd b. Müseyyeb, Urve, Kāsım, Hârice b. Zeyd ve Nâfi‘b. Cübeyr b. Mut‘im vesâir ashâb-ı kirâmdan dahi mervîdir

rows.speaker: Şu‘be
rows.claim: Shuʿba said that when he took Ibn ʿAbbās to the prayer ground, Ibn ʿAbbās questioned the crowd's takbir and asked whether the imam had begun it.
rows.anchor: Ebû Bekir Râzî Ahkâmü’l-Kur’ân’da bunları naklederken der ki: “İbn Abbas’ın mevlâsı Şu‘be şöyle demiştir:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı infers that Ibn ʿAbbās disliked takbir on the route and understood the verse as the imam's takbir in the sermon, which others may join; the crescent report does not require loudness.
rows.anchor: Bundan anlaşılır ki İbn Abbas tarîk-i musallâda tekbîri hoş görmemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred Hanafi position makes none of these takbirs obligatory; a quiet takbir at the Eid crescent is recommended, and takbir on the way to Eid prayer is sunnah, quiet for Ramadan Eid and aloud for Sacrifice Eid.
rows.anchor: mezheb-i Hanefî’de muhtâr olan şudur ki bu tekbirlerin hiçbiri vâcib değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the verse implies an obligatory takbir at Eid's arrival, Elmalılı says it can mean the Eid prayer and its takbirs: complete Ramadan, glorify God, and pray Eid.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde hâsıl-ı ma‘nâ: “Ramazanı ikmal edip tekbir alarak bayram namazını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing gratitude points especially to celebrating Eid as thanksgiving and connects the fasting passage with the earlier commands to eat and give thanks in 2:172.
rows.anchor: Ve bu suretle farîza-i sıyâmın tâ yukarıdaki كُلُوا وَاشْكُرُوا [bk. el-Bakara 2/172] emirlerine tenâsuku

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the verse's linked clauses contain arguments that refute the Jabriyya.
rows.anchor: bu âyette Cebriyye mezhebini ibtal edecek deliller vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports that a Bedouin asked the Prophet whether God was near, so they should pray privately, or far, so they should call aloud.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunduğuna göre a‘rabînin birisi Resûlullah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı presents the following verse as God's reply identifying the deity worthy of takbir and gratitude, stressing supplication's close relation to fasting and obedience to its rulings.
rows.anchor: duanın savma şiddet-i münâsebetini ifham ve ahkâmının mer‘iyyet-i icrâsını emr için telvîn-i hitâb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı explains manāsik here as the acts of worship connected with Hajj and locates the ensuing remembrance command in the days at Minā.
rows.anchor: menâsikinizi, yani hacca müte‘allik ibadetlerinizi bitirdiğinizde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Islam, Arabs stayed at Minā after Hajj between the mosque and mountain, recalling their ancestors' glories and notable days; this verse replaces that custom with remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: Kable’l-İslâm Araplar âdetleri vechile menâsik-i haccı bitirdikten sonra Minâ’da mescid ile dağ arasındaki mevkide tevakkuf ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command sustains Hajj's sacred spiritual awakening; stoning the devil and saying takbir are its final, cherished reminders.
rows.anchor: şeytan taşlamak ve tekbirler almak, bunun son bir hâtıra-i bergüzîdesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hajj rites enact the denial of association with God, making the practical implications of the declaration of divine unity visible.
rows.anchor: kelime-i tevhiddeki nefy-i şirk mânası bütün levâzım-ı ameliyesiyle fiilen gösterilmiş oluyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hajj should lead beyond ancestral memory and personal, family, or tribal pride: its hardships and sacred history teach human frailty and the transience of the world before God's permanence.
rows.anchor: fânîlerin aczlerini, bâkīnin sırr-ı bekāsını sezen âkil ü kâmil insanların bu ibadetten alacakları intibâh-ı rûhî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proper spiritual outcome is to cast off traces of shirk, pride, sensual drives, and false impressions, then live in prayer, repentance, dependence, and continual remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: her türlü âsâr-ı şirki atıp vahdet-i külliyeye doğru yürümek nefsin gurûr-ı şahsî ve ailevî ve kavmîsini

words: فَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some people ask only for worldly provision, with all their aspiration fixed on this life and no requested or expected share in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: bütün himmeti dünyaya maksurdur.

words: فَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا
rows.speaker: İmam Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Rāzī classifies happiness as spiritual, bodily, and external; each has two forms: knowledge and virtue, health and beauty, wealth and status.
rows.anchor: İmam Fahreddin Râzî tefsîrinde der ki: “Saadetlerin merâtibi üçtür: Rûhâniye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A request for knowledge or virtue is worldly when sought for status or management of worldly affairs; those denying resurrection seek any virtue only for this life.
rows.anchor: ilim dünyada tezeyyün ve akrâna tekaddüm için talep edilirse dünyadan olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders al-khamr as wine and al-maysir as gambling.
rows.anchor: sana hamr ü meysirden, şarab ve kumardan soruyorlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUmar, Muʿādh, and other Companions asked the Prophet for a ruling on wine because it removes the intellect; this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer ve Muâz ile beraber sahâbeden birtakım zevat idi “Yâ Resûlallah, hamr hakkında bize bir fetvâ ver çünkü aklı gideriyor” dediler ve bu âyet nâzil oldu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamr originally means covering; specifically it names fermented grape juice after its foam subsides because it covers the intellect or clouds the head.
rows.anchor: “Hamr”, esasen örtmek mânasına masdar olduğu hâlde “çiğ üzüm şırasından iştidad etmiş ve köpüğünü atmış olan şaraba isim olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By extension, hamr can mean any substance that intoxicates, so all intoxicants fall under the word in its broad sense.
rows.anchor: bu mânaca müskirâtın hepsi hamrdır.

rows.speaker: İbn Ömer
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that at the time the wine prohibition was revealed, hamr came from grapes, dates, wheat, barley, and millet, and meant what clouds the intellect.
rows.anchor: İbn Ömer hazretlerinden mervîdir ki tahrîm-i hamr nâzil olduğu gün hamr beş şeyden: üzümden, hurmadan, buğdaydan, arpadan, darıdan idi

rows.speaker: Nu‘mân b. Beşir
rows.claim: A report in Abū Dāwūd attributes to the Prophet the statement that wine is made from grapes, dates, honey, wheat, and barley.
rows.anchor: Ebû Dâvûd’da Nu‘mân b. Beşir’den rivayet olunduğu üzere Resûllullah إِنَّ مِنَ الْعِنَبِ خَمْرًا

rows.speaker: İmam Mâlik, İmam Şâfiî and many jurists
rows.claim: Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and many earlier and later jurists take hamr broadly as any intoxicant, making every kind Qurʾanically forbidden, including every drop and its trade.
rows.anchor: İmam Mâlik ve Şâfiî ve bunlardan mukaddem

rows.speaker: Ebû Hanîfe, his Companions and many early jurists
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and many early scholars say Qurʾanic hamr definitively means grape wine; other intoxicants are forbidden for intoxication by analogy and hadith, not by the word's certain scope.
rows.anchor: İmam-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretleriyle beraber ashâb ve tâbi‘înden birçok ulemâ ve fukahâ “hamr” kelimesinin beyyin ve kat‘î olan mânası bilhassa üzüm şarabı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı distinguishes the definitive Qurʾanic prohibition of grape wine from the broader possible meaning: other intoxicants are prohibited through the intoxication rationale and hadith, not the wording alone.
rows.anchor: Lafz-ı Kur’ân’ın ma‘nâ-yı e‘amma hamli muhtemil ise de ma‘nâ-yı hâssı gibi kat‘î değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grape wine and drinks made from it are intrinsically impure, and even a drop may not be consumed; impurity of other intoxicants is uncertain, so contact need not invalidate prayer.
rows.anchor: Üzüm şarabı ve bundan ma‘mul olan müskirât aynen necistir. Öbürlerinin ise necis olması şüphelidir.

rows.speaker: Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa held that a small amount of non-grape intoxicant could be drunk for strength if it did not intoxicate and was not consumed to imitate immoral people or unbelievers.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hanîfe hazretleri bu suretle şarabdan mâ‘adâ müskirâtın aynı ve katresi necis ve haram olmadığına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred Hanafi view, shared with the other three schools, follows the hadith that whatever intoxicates in a large amount is forbidden even in a small amount.
rows.anchor: muhtâr olan مَا اَسْكَرَ كَثِيرُهُ فَقَلِيلُهُ حَرَامٌ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the legal question of drinking, all intoxicants count as hamr in the broad sense; chemically, fermentation gives intoxicants a shared wine-like nature, reflected in the word alcohol.
rows.anchor: Şer‘an şürb nokta-i nazarından bütün müskirât ma‘nâyı e‘ammıyla hamrdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medicinal treatment follows the Qurʾanic concession for necessity, including needs treated as necessities.
rows.anchor: zarûret ve zarûret hükmünde bulunan ihtiyaç mesâilindendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the verse's translation, al-ʿafw is rendered as what does not burden or strain the giver.
rows.anchor: de ki sıkmayanını
